BrightLeaf: provide 3 representative client scripts and sample input dataset by 2026-06-22
Schedule 90-minute deep-dive for streaming fallbacks week of 2026-06-29

action_items: Jenna Ortiz: send benchmark template + infra checklist (due 2026-06-20)
Sana Ahmed: upload sanitized client scripts to shared repo (due 2026-06-22)
Tomás Li: prepare streaming vs batch config examples and expected metrics (due 2026-06-24)

meeting_header:
Date: 2026-06-18 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees (Redwood): Jenna Ortiz, Tomás Li, Kiran Desai
Attendees (Customer): Sana Ahmed, Marco Ruiz, Priya Patel, Ethan Cole
Notes: POC planning focused on loadshape, streaming vs non-streaming switch logic, harness integration and success criteria.
summary: Workshop-style scoping call to align on benchmark success criteria and integration points for BrightLeaf's POC. Primary goals: define workload sizing (ramp, steady, burst), decide streaming vs non-streaming approaches, agree on telemetry and acceptance thresholds, and pin initial timeline. Action items include sharing benchmark template, customer providing scripts, and scheduling a focused streaming fallback deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Ortiz: okay we can get started, thanks everyone for making time today. agenda is short — loadshape, scripts, streaming switch logic, success criteria.
[00:18] Sana Ahmed: great thanks, we want to make sure the harness runs match our real traffic which is spiky, so not just constant qps, we get huge bursts after certain events.
[00:35] Tomás Li: yeah so we usually recommend a three-phase profile: cold-start ramp, steady-state, and burst spikes; also measure tail latency separately. can you describe current client behavior?
[00:50] Marco Ruiz: sure, our clients do long-polling and some websocket flows. about 60% of requests are short chat-turns avg 12 tokens, 40% are long form generation up to 1024 tokens, but that longform is rare and causes tail.
[01:12] Kiran Desai: quick question, are you looking at streaming to reduce client perceived latency, or purely throughput optimization?
[01:20] Priya Patel: both really, product needs streaming for interactive editors. but we also need a non-streaming fallback for background batch jobs. so the harness needs to support both.
[01:36] Jenna Ortiz: perfect, so we need example scripts for both streaming and non-streaming. also important: do you have a preference hosted vs dedicate — that will change quantization and batch sizing.
[01:52] Sana Ahmed: we're leaning hosted first for time to value, but might move to dedicated if cost gets high. security team will likely ask about VPC later.
[02:03] Ethan Cole: and we will need audit logs retained for 90 days, also encryption keys via our KMS.
[02:12] Tomás Li: noted, we will include telemetry for audit log hooks. for benchmarks, we care about p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. what are your acceptance thresholds?
[02:28] Sana Ahmed: p95 < 350ms for chat-turns, p99 < 850ms ideally, and token cost not exceed our internal budget baseline — we'll attach that number to follow up.
[02:41] Marco Ruiz: also cold-start tail—under 2 seconds for initial response is important because we scale ephemeral nodes.
[02:51] [00:03:05] Kiran Desai: small note on harness: the harness supports both HTTP streaming chunks and websocket streaming; since some of your scripts are legacy, we can show a shim that toggles between streamed chunks and full-response path.
[03:15] Priya Patel: can you demo the shim?
[03:18] Tomás Li: yes in the deep-dive, for this session we'll map out expected inputs. for streaming we need to know chunk frequency and whether clients expect partial deltas vs token-by-token. some clients do token aggregation client-side which affects network overhead.
[03:39] Sana Ahmed: our editor sends deltas every 200ms, roughly 3-5 tokens per chunk typically. mobile has higher latency so they batch more.
[03:49] Jenna Ortiz: that's helpful. for loadshape, would you be able to provide a 24-hour synthetic trace or at least a representative 2-hour window?
[03:58] Marco Ruiz: yes we can pull a sanitized 2-hour trace, we'll scrub PII.
[04:05] [00:04:20] Ethan Cole: infra questions — will the harness run from our staging VPC or Redwood's hosted harness? we prefer staging VPC to hit similar egress rules.
[04:20] Tomás Li: both supported. for staging VPC we need a test token and an endpoint; we can also run Redwood's harness against your endpoint if you give network access.
[04:31] Sana Ahmed: we'll try staging VPC first.
[04:34] Kiran Desai: important: if you run from inside your VPC you'll see different latency numbers because of network egress, so we'll capture both if possible.
[04:42] [00:05:00] Tomás Li: handshake for scripts — we'll need sample client scripts in your language(s) and the input distributions: payload sizes, token distributions, and session lengths. the harness expects a small adapter that maps to our API; we can supply adapter examples in python/node/java.
[05:05] Priya Patel: most of our clients are JS and a few python backends.
[05:09] Jenna Ortiz: we'll drop a repo link with adapters. can you confirm you want streaming shim for JS?
[05:16] Priya Patel: yes please.
[05:18] [00:05:40] Marco Ruiz: about metrics: what telemetry do you need? per-request latency, per-token cost, KV-cash hit rates? (laughs) i mean kv cache hit rates.
[05:32] Tomás Li: yes KV cache hit rate, prefix cache, batch sizes, cpu/gpu util, and for streaming path we track chunk latency and chunk size distribution. also memory usage per worker.
[05:45] Sana Ahmed: and logs for any 5xxs with full request ids so we can debug.
[05:51] [00:06:10] Kiran Desai: let's capture examples for backoff policy — when model saturates, do you want automatic fallback to a smaller/quantized variant or queue with exponential backoff?
[06:02] Priya Patel: prefer fallback to smaller model for interactive, queueing for batch processes.
[06:09] Jenna Ortiz: ok, we'll propose a routing policy: interactive -> try primary -> if queue depth > X or latency > Y then route to smaller model; batch -> allow queueing up to N minutes then reject. we'll formalize thresholds in the template.
[06:24] [00:06:40] Sana Ahmed: timeline — we need initial numbers by end of next week, can you commit to that?
[06:29] Jenna Ortiz: we can do initial harness config + sample run within 48-72 hours after you send scripts and staging access. full 1-hour steady-state run and analysis within 7 days.
[06:40] Marco Ruiz: good. question on warm-up: do you recommend synthetic warm-up or replay from trace?
[06:46] Tomás Li: replay from trace is best, synthetic warm-up can still be used for stress tests. we'll document both.
[06:54] [00:07:20] Ethan Cole: security — we need SOC 2 docs and a data flow diagram, also SAML for console.
[07:04] Jenna Ortiz: yes we'll share SOC 2 summary and a redacted data flow. SAML is supported; we'll share SSO instructions in the next email.
[07:12] [00:07:50] Priya Patel: can we get an example of the cost report? like cost per 1M tokens plus overhead for streaming?
[07:19] Kiran Desai: yes the benchmark template includes cost modeling: tokens/sec, tokens per invoice unit, and streaming overhead per chunk. we'll include a worked example with your token distribution once scripts are in.
[07:34] [00:08:30] Marco Ruiz: minor nit: our billing team needs to see dev vs prod differences; can the harness tag runs for environment?
[07:40] Tomás Li: harness supports run tags and metadata. we'll include that.
[07:44] [00:09:00] Sana Ahmed: on failure modes — how does Redwood handle partial stream failures? we want guaranteed at-least-once or maybe idempotent retries.
[09:05] Tomás Li: streaming is best-effort; we recommend a token-offset resume strategy for idempotency. if partial chunk lost we re-request from last token id. we'll show an example shim.
[09:22] [00:09:40] Jenna Ortiz: for acceptance criteria recap: p95 < 350ms for chat-turns, p99 < 850ms, cold-start < 2s, throughput X (we'll fill in after we see your budget), and robust streaming fallback — agreed?
[09:55] Priya Patel: agreed, subject to final throughput budget.
[10:00] [00:10:15] Marco Ruiz: one more infra question — if we run harness from Redwood hosted, does it support GPU reservation to simulate Dedicated?
[10:25] Tomás Li: we can pin a model to a quantized variant and emulate different GPU shapes; for exact Dedicated parity we'd recommend a Dedicated trial or an autoscaling config that mimics dedicated capacity.
[10:40] [00:10:50] Kiran Desai: note: quantization will reduce cost but might impact long-form quality; we'll flag that in the evals.
[11:00] Sana Ahmed: acceptable as long as we measure quality regression with our prompt set.
[11:06] [00:11:20] Jenna Ortiz: action items and timeline — we'll circulate the template and a short checklist: staging endpoint, scripts, sample trace, and SSO requirements. after we get that we'll schedule the 90-minute streaming fallback deep dive.
[11:30] [00:11:45] Priya Patel: can you also include an example adapter for JS streaming that toggles to non-stream?
[11:52] Tomás Li: yes we'll include node/express example and a lightweight python runner.
[12:00] [00:12:00] Marco Ruiz: regarding logs, can we get a raw export of per-request latencies for the 1-hour run? that's what our perf team wants.
[12:12] Jenna Ortiz: yes raw CSV export available.
[12:18] [00:12:35] Sana Ahmed: final note — please redact any internal tokens, we'll supply test tokens.
[12:43] Jenna Ortiz: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the repo link and template. meeting adjourned.
[12:52] [END]
